subject: Deployment mode decision — latency & throughput recap
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment mode & latency/throughput signals

Samir / Elena — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the asks we captured so we can align the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Please confirm or correct anything I miss.

Key signals you shared
- Business: customer checkout flow (tokenization + fraud scoring) with strict tail-latency expectations for user experience.
- Desired latency: P95 goal ~ 100–120 ms for inference response time (end-to-end request from app to response).
- Volume: baseline ~ 300 qps, steady-hour peaks ~ 600 qps, short spikes up to ~800–1,000 qps during promos (10–15 minute windows).
- Payload: average input ~ 450 tokens; typical response ~ 80–150 tokens.
- Security: PCI-scope service; PII redaction required — procurement flagged data residency / vendor controls but engineering indicated willingness to use hosted if we can avoid logging raw payloads.

Attachments sent
- pilot_qps_profile.csv (sample traffic profile you shared) — attached for our bench team.
- redwood-hosted-dedicated-comparison.pdf (short explainer) — also attached.

Initial recommendation (high level)
- Based on the P95 target + peak spikes, Dedicated capacity is the safer path for predictable tail latency and guaranteed throughput. It gives dedicated GPU pools and prioritizes kernel selection / cache locality for low variance.
- Hosted API can work for steady-state traffic if you accept a slightly higher P95 during sudden microbursts; we can combine Hosted with a Dedicated fallback (routing policy) to handle spikes.
- Private/VPC is an option if procurement requires strict controls — we should coordinate on compliance checklist next if that becomes necessary.

Next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm the 800–1,000 qps spike duration and frequency (daily/weekly)? If you can share a 48–72h sample, our bench will model burst behavior.
2) Are there absolute SLA constraints (e.g., legal/regulatory) that mandate no external storage of payloads?
3) Are you open to an initial 2‑week Dedicated pilot (small reserved pool) + Hosted fallback to validate latency under load? We can provide a scoped quote and an ops runbook.

Proposed time for a short benchmarking sync: Tue/Wed next week — 30 minutes to align traffic windows and required SLAs.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa (SE) to scope the bench.

—
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcheckout.com>

Cc: Elena Gomez <elena@fastcheckout.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode & latency/throughput signals

Thanks Karthik — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Spike behavior: spikes to ~900–1,000 qps happen roughly 2–3 times per week for ~8–12 minutes (marketing-triggered flashes). We also see daily morning peaks ~600 qps.
- SLA: product team wants customer-facing P95 <=120ms. Procurement is nervous about anything that could be interpreted as storing cardholder data; they asked if Redwood hosted would keep any payloads. Our engineering note: we can strip card numbers before sending, but we still send session metadata and device signals.
- Compliance: if you support a Private/VPC deployment we can keep everything inside our VPC, but that adds procurement time — they asked for a TCO comparison.

Can you send a rough sketch of throughput cost for Dedicated vs Hosted for a pilot-sized commit (2 weeks, baseline 300 qps, with spikes to 1k)? Also, if we go Dedicated, can you confirm whether autoscaling across GPUs will cover short spikes or if we need explicit burst capacity?

If useful, Elena and I are available Wed 31 Jul 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 1 Aug afternoon.

Samir
VP Product, FastCheckout
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode & latency/throughput signals

Samir — quick technical note from SE perspective to help separate the tradeoffs and propose a concrete pilot.

Short answers to your asks
- Cost sketch: we’ll send a concise pilot TCO in the follow-up (separately) but high level: Dedicated (reserved) will have a higher up-front commit but predictable per-request cost under sustained load and lower tail latency variance. Hosted is lower commitment but may show slightly flatter latency improvements during microbursts unless paired with Dedicated burst nodes.
- Autoscaling: Redwood Dedicated supports autoscaling across GPU pools, but 8–12 minute flash spikes of 900–1,000 qps are better handled with a small pre-warmed burst pool (we can size this) + autoscaler; pure reactive scaling may not converge quickly enough for <15 minute spikes.
- Data handling: Hosted API can be configured with zero-persistence mode (no request logging, zero retention) and payload redaction hooks; however procurement often prefers VPC for complete network isolation.

Pilot proposal (concrete)
1) Two-week pilot combining: 1x small Dedicated pool sized for sustained 600 qps + 1x small pre-warmed burst pool that absorbs 900–1,000 qps spikes.
2) Route main traffic to Hosted API by default (quick cutover) with automatic routing policy to Dedicated when the spike window triggers or latency crosses threshold. This gives you the speed of Hosted for typical traffic and the predictability of Dedicated for spikes.
3) Bench plan: Redwood will run two synthetic benches (baseline and flash-spike) against your sample profile (pilot_qps_profile.csv). On the bench we’ll capture P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.

Deliverables
- Scoped pilot quote + runbook (contract language suitable for procurement)
- Bench report within 5 business days after we get the 72h traffic sample
- Ops playbook for routing policy and rollback

Link to a short explainer: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-pilot-docs (I’ve dropped a brief Hosted vs Dedicated comparison there).

If Wed 31 Jul 10:00 PT works we’ll schedule the bench sync; otherwise Thu afternoon is fine.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
